comments: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance
formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case.
Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.
Perturb a_1 → 1 + δ, δ ~ N(0, σ²). The analytical first-order GUM
variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

Two defects sat here, and the second hid behind the first:
1. Assignment REBOUND the local's variance/sens to the RHS's fresh vregs
instead of copying into fixed slots. A rebind is a compile-time map update
and a loop body's IR is emitted once, so every iteration recomputed from
the pre-loop uncertainty and only one iteration's contribution survived.
2. The fix for (1) allocated those slots BEFORE the branches that bind a
declaration's variance from its RHS, so those branches overwrote them.
Only a literal-initialised local escaped, because a literal leaves those
branches nothing to bind.
Truth values below are first-order GUM propagation, computed independently
rather than read off either engine. var(cl) = 1.24^2 = 1.5376.
TEST 1 deliberately uses NO loop. The defect never needed one — a loop only
turned a wrong answer into a catastrophic one. Four loop-based repros failed to
separate the two causes; three straight-line assignments did it immediately.
If this pin ever regresses, TEST 1 is the one that localises it.

fn embed_axis(hash: i64) -> i64 {
    let r: i64 = hash - (hash / 7) * 7
    return 1 + r
}

fn embed_into(hash: i64, out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        out[i as usize] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    out[0] = 0.6
    out[embed_axis(hash) as usize] = 0.8
}

fn oct_mul(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, NonAssoc {
    var r0 = a[0] * b[0]
    r0 = r0 - a[1] * b[1]
    r0 = r0 - a[2] * b[2]
    r0 = r0 - a[3] * b[3]
    r0 = r0 - a[4] * b[4]
    r0 = r0 - a[5] * b[5]
    r0 = r0 - a[6] * b[6]
    r0 = r0 - a[7] * b[7]
    out[0] = r0

    var r1 = a[0] * b[1] + a[1] * b[0]
    r1 = r1 + a[2] * b[3] - a[3] * b[2]
    r1 = r1 + a[4] * b[5] - a[5] * b[4]
    r1 = r1 - a[6] * b[7] + a[7] * b[6]
    out[1] = r1

    var r2 = a[0] * b[2] + a[2] * b[0]
    r2 = r2 - a[1] * b[3] + a[3] * b[1]
    r2 = r2 + a[4] * b[6] - a[6] * b[4]
    r2 = r2 + a[5] * b[7] - a[7] * b[5]
    out[2] = r2

    var r3 = a[0] * b[3] + a[3] * b[0]
    r3 = r3 + a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1]
    r3 = r3 + a[4] * b[7] - a[7] * b[4]
    r3 = r3 - a[5] * b[6] + a[6] * b[5]
    out[3] = r3

    var r4 = a[0] * b[4] + a[4] * b[0]
    r4 = r4 - a[1] * b[5] + a[5] * b[1]
    r4 = r4 - a[2] * b[6] + a[6] * b[2]
    r4 = r4 - a[3] * b[7] + a[7] * b[3]
    out[4] = r4

    var r5 = a[0] * b[5] + a[5] * b[0]
    r5 = r5 + a[1] * b[4] - a[4] * b[1]
    r5 = r5 - a[2] * b[7] + a[7] * b[2]
    r5 = r5 + a[3] * b[6] - a[6] * b[3]
    out[5] = r5

    var r6 = a[0] * b[6] + a[6] * b[0]
    r6 = r6 + a[1] * b[7] - a[7] * b[1]
    r6 = r6 + a[2] * b[4] - a[4] * b[2]
    r6 = r6 - a[3] * b[5] + a[5] * b[3]
    out[6] = r6

    var r7 = a[0] * b[7] + a[7] * b[0]
    r7 = r7 - a[1] * b[6] + a[6] * b[1]
    r7 = r7 + a[2] * b[5] - a[5] * b[2]
    r7 = r7 + a[3] * b[4] - a[4] * b[3]
    out[7] = r7
}

fn oct_associator(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], c: &[f64; 8], out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, NonAssoc {
    var ab: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var ab_c: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var bc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var a_bc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_mul(a, b, &!ab)
    oct_mul(&ab, c, &!ab_c)
    oct_mul(b, c, &!bc)
    oct_mul(a, &bc, &!a_bc)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        out[i as usize] = ab_c[i as usize] - a_bc[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn norm_sq(v: &[f64; 8]) -> f64 {
    return v[0]*v[0] + v[1]*v[1] + v[2]*v[2] + v[3]*v[3]
         + v[4]*v[4] + v[5]*v[5] + v[6]*v[6] + v[7]*v[7]
}

fn alt_stat_sq(x: &[f64; 8], y: &[f64; 8]) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var assoc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_associator(x, x, y, &!assoc)
    let den_sq: f64 = norm_sq(x) * norm_sq(x) * norm_sq(y)
    if den_sq < 0.0000000000000001 { return 0.0 }
    return norm_sq(&assoc) / den_sq
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var hashes: [i64; 8] = [100, 200, 100, 300, 200, 400, 300, 500]
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < 8 {
            if hashes[i as usize] == hashes[j as usize] {
                var x: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
                var y: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
                embed_into(hashes[i as usize], &!x)
                embed_into(701 + i + j, &!y)
                sum = sum + alt_stat_sq(&x, &y)
                count = count + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var ok: i64 = 1
    var stat_sq: f64 = 0.0
    if count > 0 { stat_sq = sum / (count as f64) }
    if count == 0 { ok = 0 }
    if stat_sq >= 0.000000000000000000000001 { ok = 0 }

    if ok == 1 { print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }
    return 0
}

Before this fix, a var mutated inside a while loop would have its VAR_CH_SET

the snapshot+union was missing.  After the fix:
1. VAR_CH_SET is snapshotted before the loop runs (so 0-iteration loops

and post-loop channels — sound conservative upper bound).

that the channel gained in the loop body is present in the post-loop topology.

and the quotient rule fed by a composite numerator.

row. Each row prints its value and its own verdict, and the summary sentinel
is printed only when every row passed.

scalar value channel. Composition lives in user-space algebra (oct_mul) and
re-wraps via `Knowledge { value: ... }`. That is the F functor's intended shape.

comments: Regression test (segfault landmine, discovered via PR #2058):
A string literal passed as a function-call argument is embedded directly
in the generated code with a "jmp over the bytes, then lea rax back at
them" trick. The x86-64 codegen used a rel8 (single signed byte, -128..127)
displacement for that skip jump. Any literal whose decoded content was
>= 127 bytes made the skip distance overflow the byte, wrapping negative
and sending execution backward into unrelated, already-emitted code --
corrupting whatever ran next. The callee was never reached; the crash hit
while the *caller* was still setting up the argument.
This exercises a literal well past that threshold (~200 bytes) as a call
argument, and checks the callee receives the exact content -- not just
that the process survives.

adaptive effect without rollback — the next step's dt is informed by the

Deep-research (peer-reviewed: Gresnigt et al., EPJC 2019 s10052-019-6967-1 / 2024 s10052-024-13476-0;
arXiv 2306.13098) establishes: the left-multiplication algebra of the complexified sedenions ℂ⊗𝕊 is
the Clifford algebra Cℓ(8) ≅ ℂ(16) (256 = 2^8 maps), the rank-4 step up from the octonionic Cℓ(6)
(64 = 2^6) that underlies Furey's one-generation SM construction. This test certifies the Clifford
PRESENTATION exactly: the eight left-multiplication operators L_1..L_8 pairwise anticommute and each
squares to −I — eight anticommuting √(−I) generators = a Cℓ(8) presentation. The 8th generator is
L_8 = e_8, the octonion→sedenion doubling unit (so e_8 is exactly the extra Clifford generator).
Uses the SPARSE identity: e_i·e_k = σ(i,k)·e_{i⊕k}, so L_i has one entry σ(i,k) per column k at row
i⊕k. Then (L_i L_j)[r][c] = σ(i,j⊕c)σ(j,c) at row r=i⊕j⊕c, giving:

// Build a main that loads f64 1.5 into rdi and calls print_f64, then exit(0)
fn emit_main(code: CodeBuffer, print_f64_off: i64) -> CodeBuffer with Mut {
    var c = code
    // mov rax, IEEE754(1.5) = 0x3FF8000000000000
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x48); c = emit_byte(c, 0xb8)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0xf8); c = emit_byte(c, 0x3f)
    // mov rdi, rax
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x48); c = emit_byte(c, 0x89); c = emit_byte(c, 0xc7)
    // call print_f64 (rel32)
    let call_site = c.len
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xe8)
    let rel = print_f64_off - (call_site + 5)
    c = emit_byte(c, rel & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 8) & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 16) & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 24) & 0xFF)
    // mov edi, 0 (exit code)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xbf); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    // mov eax, 60 (sys_exit)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xb8); c = emit_byte(c, 0x3c); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    // syscall
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x0f); c = emit_byte(c, 0x05)
    c
}

fn emit_u16(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b
}

fn emit_u32(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 2) as usize] = ((v >> 16) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 3) as usize] = ((v >> 24) & 0xFF) as i8

fn emit_u64(buf: [i8; 4096], off: i64, v: i64) -> [i8; 4096] with Mut {
    var b = buf
    b[(off) as usize] = (v & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 1) as usize] = ((v >> 8) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 2) as usize] = ((v >> 16) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 3) as usize] = ((v >> 24) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 4) as usize] = ((v >> 32) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 5) as usize] = ((v >> 40) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 6) as usize] = ((v >> 48) & 0xFF) as i8
    b[(off + 7) as usize] = ((v >> 56) & 0xFF) as i8

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Build code: print_f64 at offset 0, then main stub
    var code = code_buffer_new()
    code = ast_emit_print_f64_builtin(code)
    let main_off = code.len
    code = emit_main(code, 0)  // print_f64 is at code offset 0

    let code_size = code.len
    let vaddr_base: i64 = 0x400000
    let code_file_off: i64 = 0x80  // After ELF header (64 bytes) + 1 program header (56 bytes) = 120 = 0x78, round up
    let entry_vaddr = vaddr_base + code_file_off + main_off

    // Build minimal ELF64 header
    var elf: [i8; 4096] = [0; 4096]

    // ELF magic: 7f 45 4c 46
    elf[0 as usize] = 0x7f as i8
    elf[1 as usize] = 0x45 as i8  // E
    elf[2 as usize] = 0x4c as i8  // L
    elf[3 as usize] = 0x46 as i8  // F

    // EI_CLASS=2 (64-bit), EI_DATA=1 (LE), EI_VERSION=1, EI_OSABI=0
    elf[4 as usize] = 2 as i8
    elf[5 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[6 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[7 as usize] = 0 as i8

    // e_type=2 (ET_EXEC), e_machine=0x3E (x86-64)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 16, 2)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 18, 0x3E)
    // e_version=1
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 20, 1)
    // e_entry
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 24, entry_vaddr)
    // e_phoff = 64 (right after ELF header)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 32, 64)
    // e_shoff = 0 (no section headers)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 40, 0)
    // e_flags = 0
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 48, 0)
    // e_ehsize = 64
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 52, 64)
    // e_phentsize = 56
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 54, 56)
    // e_phnum = 1
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 56, 1)
    // e_shentsize = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 58, 0)
    // e_shnum = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 60, 0)
    // e_shstrndx = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 62, 0)

    // Program header (LOAD) at offset 64
    // p_type = 1 (PT_LOAD)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 64, 1)
    // p_flags = 5 (PF_R | PF_X)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 68, 5)
    // p_offset = 0
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 72, 0)
    // p_vaddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 80, vaddr_base)
    // p_paddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 88, vaddr_base)
    // p_filesz = code_file_off + code_size
    let total_file = code_file_off + code_size
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 96, total_file)
    // p_memsz = total_file
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 104, total_file)
    // p_align = 0x1000
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 112, 0x1000)

    // Copy code bytes into ELF at code_file_off
    var ci: i64 = 0
    while ci < code_size {
        elf[(code_file_off + ci) as usize] = code.bytes[ci as usize]
        ci = ci + 1
    }

    let elf_size = code_file_off + code_size

    // Write ELF to file using VM builtin
    let wr = write_file("/tmp/sprint235_f64.elf", elf, elf_size)
    if wr < 0 {
        print("FAIL: could not write ELF\n")
        return 1
    }

    print("PASS: ELF written size=")
    print_int(elf_size)
    print(" entry=0x")
    print_int(entry_vaddr)
    print(" code=")
    print_int(code_size)
    print("\n")
    0
}

The signed domain gave Sub an escape hatch: a non-disjoint pair is ALLOWED
when ns_cov_nonneg proves every shared source carries a non-negative
coefficient product. That certificate is only as good as the signs feeding
it, and the transfer originally sent every operator except Sub, Mul and Div
through ns_union -- the ADDITIVE join. OpRem landed there. So
r = a % b        published a's and b's additive signs as if they were r's
s = r - a        found `a` at + in both operands, certified Cov >= 0,
and COMPILED
but Rem's Jacobian signs are not the additive join of its operands' signs, so
that certificate was unfounded and Var(r - a) could be understated -- the
exact thing E230 exists to refuse, reintroduced through the new escape hatch
rather than through the rule it guards.
The fix makes ns_union_opaque the DEFAULT and ns_union the exception (OpAdd
only): an operator nobody has modelled marks its result sign-unknown, and
ns_cov_nonneg fails closed on it. This file must stay refused. If it ever
compiles again, the transfer has gone back to trusting signs it cannot derive.

The pattern used to read E001, which this program never emits — it is rejected
by the refinement checker with an uncoded diagnostic. The harness was not
matching error-pattern at all, so the test passed while asserting the wrong
thing; with the matcher fixed the annotation had to say what is actually
emitted.
`requires: lean_single` because the diagnostic this asserts is an engine
difference, not a language rule. Measured 2026-09-03 on both:
lean_single  error[E208]: refinement type violation — value 0 does not
satisfy parameter predicate at line 19        ← what is asserted
Madaros      error[E008] return value does not match declared return type
error[E001] this binding expects a different type
error[E009] argument type does not match parameter
Madaros is not missing the diagnostic — check.sio carries code 42, "value does
not satisfy the refinement predicate". It never reaches it, because it relates
a refinement type to its base type in NEITHER direction:
fn f(x: Positive) -> i32 { x }    E008, though every Positive IS an i32
let p: Positive = 0               E001, a bare type mismatch standing where
the predicate should have spoken
So the three errors above are all one gap wearing three codes, and the E009 at
the call site rejects for the wrong reason: NonNeg and Positive differ as
NAMES, not because 0 fails `n > 0`. Two identical refinement names with a
violated predicate would slip through it.
Erasure (Positive → i32) would be sound to open on its own. The introduction
direction is where the predicate must actually be evaluated, and opening it
without first proving the check fires would turn a wrongly-coded rejection
into an acceptance — a fail-open in a type system. Left for whoever implements
refinement subsumption in the modular checker, rather than half-done here.
